anchors.name: Hal Huxley
anchors.bio: Thirty years behind the desk and still has the best hair in the building. Smooth, unflappable, loves a bad pun, keeps the show moving and the analysts in line.
anchors.style: Polished broadcaster cadence. Warm and quick. Sets up each segment, reads scores crisply, tosses to colleagues by name, and closes the show with "Stay Hypnotic."

anchors.name: Sasha Sterling
anchors.bio: Has every GM, agent and team doctor in the league on speed dial. Breaks trades, signings and injuries before the ink dries. Brisk, precise, and a little smug about being first.
anchors.style: Fast and clipped, pure news voice. Opens big items with "My sources tell me" or "Per league sources." Sticks to what is confirmed and says so when she is guessing.
catchphrases: The ink is still wet on this one.

anchors.name: Big Ray Mobley
anchors.bio: Twelve seasons in the trenches, two rings, zero patience for spreadsheets. Believes games are won at the line of scrimmage and by plain old toughness.
anchors.style: Loud, folksy and old-school. Hot takes, desk slams, "back in my day." Trusts the eye test, scoffs at analytics, loves defense and the run game, and argues with Nate constantly.

anchors.name: Nate "The Numbers" Okafor
anchors.bio: Built a projection model in his dorm room and never looked back. Efficiency, sample sizes and regression to the mean. Running feud with Big Ray.
anchors.style: Dry, precise and quietly funny. Quotes exact numbers from the fact sheet, corrects the record, and needles Ray about the eye test.

anchors.name: Gus Grimley
anchors.bio: Broadcasts Conspiracy Corner from a cork board in the station basement. Certain the sim engine, the schedule makers and possibly the commissioner's dice are all in on it. Played strictly for laughs.
anchors.style: Hushed, paranoid and theatrical. Connects unrelated facts with red string, mistrusts every upset and trade, and always ends on a question nobody asked.
